title: Three poets in a crowded shelter
hookLine: rain, a dark narrow shelter, three strangers pressed together, and then a fourth who wasn't there before
carry: bhakti: love for god is its own fruit
tomorrow: a glint in the wet sand. silver, or only a shell?

cards: Rain is coming down hard at night. A wandering devotee ducks into a tiny shelter by a house. A second traveler knocks, and the first makes room.
A third arrives, soaked, and the two make room again, and now they stand shoulder to shoulder. And then, tradition says, they feel a fourth pressing in among them, someone none of them can see.
That's the story told of the first Alvars, the Tamil singers of Vishnu. Today's summit sit climbs back to the bhakti stretch, and the lamps those three lit.

teach.h: A LAMP MADE OF THE WORLD.
teach.b: In the story, each sings a verse to light the dark. The first, Poygai, makes a lamp of the world: the earth for its bowl, the ocean for its oil, the sun for its flame.
The second, Bhutam, makes a lamp of the heart: love for the bowl, longing for the oil, a melting mind for the wick. And the third, Pey, by that light, says simply: I have seen.
The Lord is there, with the goddess, in the crowded dark. Now hold that next to the Narada Bhakti Sutras, the short book the year read whole.
Its boldest claim is that bhakti, love for God, isn't the road to something else. It is where the road goes.

teach.h: A TASTE THAT CAN'T BE TOLD.
teach.b: And when the sutras try to say what that love is like, they give up gracefully: it can't be told, like a taste in the mouth of someone who can't speak. You can have it. You can't hand it over in words.
From up here, the shelter and the sutras say one thing in two keys. The singers don't argue their way to God.
They light lamps and look, and the lamps are made of what they already have: the whole world, for one, their own love, for another.
Then think of the women of the bhakti stretch, and the singers of the regions: a tailor, a cobbler, a weaver, singing to God in a home language. The shelter was too small.
They made room anyway. And that, the story says, is when God pressed in.

how: The hymns of the Alvars are sung in Sri Vaishnava temples and homes in Tamil Nadu, and the Narada Bhakti Sutras are studied and recited by devotees of many bhakti traditions.

o: a look back from the top at bhakti and the Alvars' lamps
a debate where the best singer wins a royal prize
a lamp festival held each autumn in Tamil temples

games.q: lamps in the dark — tap the pairs.
p: a lamp made of the world
a lamp made of love and longing
by that light: I have seen

s: the three Alvars lit oil lamps in the shelter
in the story, they lit lamps of verse: one made of the world, one made of love.
the Narada Bhakti Sutras say bhakti is a road to something higher
they say love is where the road goes: its own fruit.
the sutras compare this love to a taste that someone who can't speak can't describe
it can be had, they say, but not told.

games.q: you're sheltering from the rain in a space that barely fits two. a third traveler knocks, soaked. what do you do?
o: go back out into the rain.
games.why: in the story, they make room and stand together. then they feel a fourth press in among them, and each sings a lamp into the dark.

practice: Notice how full the mind is, the way the shelter was full, and without pushing anything out, make a little room on each out-breath, the way the first traveler shifted over for the second.
If you pray, let that room be for God, as the Alvars felt someone press in; if you don't, let it be room for whoever comes next today.

wordCard.voice: The summit sit. One stretch of the year, seen from the top. Today's stretch: bhakti, the Alvars' lamps in a crowded shelter, and a love the sutras call its own fruit. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: bhakti, devotion, love for God.

carryVoice: Your line: bhakti, love for God, is its own fruit. A small shelter, and still room for one more. Until tomorrow.
